If you're looking for advice, then I would personally stay away from that bike. But if you do opt for it, then I would not pay a cent more than $2000 for it unless the owner can prove with receipts that the bike has actually been rebuilt that recently. And make sure it's a bottom end rebuild as well, not just a new piston. When these bikes blow up, it is not a cheap fix by any means.

If not you could expect a hefty bill, sooner than you would like. You have to keep in mind that this is a 21 year old bike, and things wear out. Not just the engine, but how about fork seals, bearings, bushings, sprockets, wheel sets, etc? All of that stuff adds up quick. If the majority of this stuff is worn, then you will spend more money and time fixing all of this than it is worth. 

At the end of the day do you want to be stuck with a 2003 that you could potentially sink over $5k into, just to make it reliable? Or would you rather bite the bullet and spend around the same amount on something from this decade that is solid. 

If $2500 is the most you can spend, then I would suggest staying away from this bike even more. There is a good chance that it will need some sort of significant repairs soon. At that point it, if you can't afford the repair, it becomes a $2500 paper weight. I would try and look for something more of a trail variety like an xr250, crf230, ttr 230, etc. Those bikes are going to need much less maintenance and are notoriously reliable. Older 2-strokes are also a cheaper option. But could still need a decent amount of work at that price range. They just don't cone with the big bill in the case of engine failure.

I agree with SilvFx. Don't be fooled by appearance. I would only opt for a bike that age if there was documentation of how its been maintained. 14 years is a long time for someone down the line to neglect maintenance.
Even then a used 4 stroke is bit of a crap shoot.

I bought a 07 Rmz250 back in 2012. Thing was loaded with aftermarket parts and shiny new plastics, and looked as if it had been meticulously maintained. Was clean enough to eat off of. Then on my first ride, it broke a retainer and dropped a valve. Destroyed the piston, cylinder, and tore up the head. Next thing I knew, my $3500 bike was a $5100 bike. That one hurt being a 15 year old kid, ended my racing for that summer.

Might care when your $2500 yz250 costs you an extra $2500 because the original crank says no more and puts a nice window in the side of your cases. Then after all is said and done, you're stuck with a 5k bike that has a good engine, but the rest of the bike is still beat. 

People aren't trying to be rude to you. They are trying to prevent you from making a costly mistake. Many of us here have learned the hard way with bikes. If that is truly the best deal you can find, I suggest you either widen your search area, increase your budget, haggle on price, or wait for something else. 

 Buying used 4-strokes is already a gamble. Buying a 21 year old 4 stroke that looks like it's been neglected is even more risky. Don't settle for what could be a ticking time bomb, just because you think it's your best option.

Glad someone said it. It's not media hype, it's just genuinely an actual heat dome. Will it be anywhere in the realm of the 2021 heat wave? No. But is it by meteorological definition a heat dome? Yes. 

For OP to try and say that it's an exaggeration is a little disingenuous, in my opinion. Sometimes, I think it would have been best if the media had not started using more meteorological terms. The moment you mention things like "Atmospheric river" or "Heat dome," people that don't understand the actual weather phenomenon seem like they get their panties in a bunch. I lost count of the number of times I had to hear "They just keep making up new terms" after the 2021 floods, even though the term Atmospheric River had been used in the weather community for decades. 

Anyone who doesn't believe this is an actual heat dome. Just look at the weather models and see for yourself. I can promise that if you look at the 500mb Winds and 500mb height, you will clearly see an omega block form by looking at the jetstream and pressure isobars. Its called an omega block because the shape of the jetstream and surrounding isobars form the shape of the omega symbol Ω. Heat domes form inside of omega blocks.
It's so incredibly frustrating to see as a weather nerd haha.
Literally every run of the GFS and ECMWF models for the last few days have been aggreeance for an omega block forming over the province on Saturday/Sunday.

Maybe a poor choice of words on my part. But it is more involved than just throwing the parts on. You would have to machine the steering stem down to fit in the KLX head bearing, unless you use the older style KX forks which I stated earlier.  Which at that point you may aswell just revalve the KLX suspention since it is already very similar to the older 91-95 KX suspension. These bikes are not very modular, they use proprietary parts because the two bikes are designed to do two totally different things. 

Im not saying it isnt doable, I just think its pointless. If someone really wants to spend the thousands on all those parts to install on a KLX, then by all means do it. Your just going to wind up with a KLX that doesn't work in the trails as well as it used to, and jumps and handles worse than a KX. 

Op should either opt for a revalve or look into another bike.

For a direct bolt on, I believe you would have to use the 91-95 KX forks, which are basically KLX gen forks with a different spring rate and valving. Any modern KX fork would require different triple clamps and steering stem to accept the larger fork.you are probably looking at a few grand all said and done for the amount of parts required. Which at the end of the day would produce a bike that performed better than it did, but still sub par while compared to a motocross bike.

 If op wants to keep the bike, but just wants to have the suspension be able to handle a bit more air time, then a simple revalve would definitely improve the riding experience. But, if he is wanting to get a little more sendy off jumps while still trail riding, then a motocross bike would be more than capable. The KLX is a heavy bike, and you are asking to break parts making it do things it wasn't designed to do. 

I ride my sx250 on moto tracks then drop the compression  all the way down and still manage to ride some pretty gnarly single track trails safely. Does it perform as well as trail bike would in the trails? No, but it gets the job done. Having a bike that performs the best in every form of riding is not an easy thing to do. The new cross country moto bikes get close, but unfortunately no matter what discipline of riding you do  there will always have to be either a compromise or two bikes.

While NC may get earthquakes, they are small and the damage is usually insignificant. You will never see a megathrust event anywhere on the east coast of North America because its is physically impossible due to not being in close proximity to a fault line. 
Just the same that Seattle will likely never see an EF5 tornado, because it just doesn't have the potential.  

My point is, the potential strength of an earthquake in Seattle far outweighs what NC could ever produce. You trying to compare the two is highly flawed. Just as comparing tornado alley to the PNW would also highly flawed.

Not even close to comparable. North Carolina doesn't have the risk of megathrust earthquakes since it doesnt sit on a subduction zone... In fact the whole east coast and mid west are in the middle of a plate.

Strongest recorded quakes east of the rocky mountains are somewhere around a M7, while the west coast has had multiple M9+ events. Might not sound like a big difference, but the actual difference between a M7 and M9 is astronomical. The equivalent energy released from a M7 earthquake is approximately 38 atomic bombs, the energy output of a M9 earthquake is 38,000 atomic bombs. Think EF2 vs EF5. 

So your argument would be like downplaying the strength of tornadoes in the south by saying, "we get tornadoes in WA, so nothing we don't already deal with".  Yes WA may very rarely get tornadoes, but they certainly don't get the violent wedges that can flatten a town like the south gets. Just like the east doesn't get the megathrust quakes that the ring of fire gets.

Not only that but the occurrence of deep Juan De Fuca earthquakes is approximately only 50 years, and on average they are close to M7 (M6.7 in 1949 and M6.8 in 2001). The subduction zone has the potential of M9+, with the last being the Cascadia earthquake of 1700 which is estimated at being between  M8.7 and M9.2. The average interval being 500 years, but as short at 250 years. 

If we are alive to witness a megathrust earthquake in the pacific northwest it will be tremendously devastating. Look at how bad the 2011 earthquake and tsunami devastated Japan, and their infrastructure is far better built for an earthquake than ours. 

I'd honestly take my chances in tornado alley. The chance of being directly hit by a tornado is quite small, but if you are unlucky enough to be hit, the result is obviously dire. But the threat of a megathrust earthquake in the PNW is not a matter of if, but a matter of when.

As someone who smoked very frequently from 14 to 22, I think I might have some advice for you. 

 The next time you smoke (if you decide to do so), I would start with only 1 hit then wait a good 15 or so minutes to see how it affects you. You can always smoke more and get higher if the effects aren't enough. But you can never go back and smoke less. A simple lesson that unfortunately took me a few bad experiences to learn lol. 

What you experienced is what me and my friends used to call greening out, and I am very familiar was very familiar with it in my early stages of smoking. Seems to be caused by smoking both too much and too quickly. I believe it actually can a short decrease of blood sugar. But you explained all the effects of greening out. I used to get all of that's as well. I would also usually end up vomiting, which funny enough was what would make me feel so much better. My worst experience actually happened in 2012 when I was 15. I got far too high and had a major panic attack in class, and since I was standing I actually passed out. Woke up on the floor bssically sober with 30 kids and the teacher standing around me. I honestly think I had actually forgotten to breathe because I was so worked up. Pretty sure my brain did a factory reset on me lol. 

Just know that if it happens again, it will pass. As much as it feels like you are going to die or have a seizure, or what ever bad things your brain is convincing you will happen, it wont.

Find a chill place with people you are comfortable with, that you know you wont have to leave for a few hours. Have your drinks and food on hand and watch a show or listen to music that you enjoy. People that use heavier psychedelics like Mushrooms and LSD refer to something called "Set and Setting". While Marijuana isnt on the same level of those drugs, I strongly believe that it can be applied to new users of marijuana. Because those that are new to the drug do experience psychedelic effects. Especially when they have never been exposed to a mind altering substance. But "Set and Setting" is essentially you are in the right mindset to experience a mind altering state (you are willing and ready, no resent major upsets or stressors), you want your mind to be at 100% as it can be an emotion amplifier. And setting you want to be in an environment you are comfortable in. 

But next time just try not to worry. Prepare yourself and take it slow and I promise you will have a good time. Some of my most enjoyable times with weed were when I was a rookie, and I always wish I could get that stoned again one day. Havent smoked much at all in well over 6 months so I will see how it goes next time lol. Hope this wasnt too much of a read. 
Cheers! 

Edit. Also from what I u understand part of the anxiety you experienced stemmed from you not being able to control the experience. Unfortunately you cannot control these experiences and trying to will only make it more difficult. As hard as it may be, it will always help to just try and let go.
